# Writing clear README files for research data and code

## Overview

This one hour workshop introduces you to best practices in research
documentation, with a focus on README files. A README is a short text file that
sits alongside your data or code and tells other people what it is, how it was
made and how to use it. A clear README supports reproducibility, collaboration
and reuse.

The workshop combines short presentations with interactive exercises. We will
look at examples of strong and weak READMEs and use guidance from Cornell Data
Services on what to include. In small groups, you will draft a README from a
short case study dataset. A second example, this time of code, will be shown and appraised. The session finishes with discussion and optional feedback on
your own projects.

The examples are from ecology and environmental research, but the concepts are
applicable to any field. No specialist software or preparation is required.

## Audience

This workshop is intended for students, early-career researchers and
practitioners in ecology and environmental sciences who produce data or code as
part of their work. No advanced technical experience is required. It is suitable
for those new to coding and for more experienced researchers who want better
documentation practices.

The materials use plain language and are provided on this website in an
accessible digital format. The activities are done in groups so that you can
support each other and take part at a level that is comfortable for you.

## Learning objectives

Participants will learn how to:

-   Explain why a README matters for reproducibility, collaboration and reuse.
-   Recognise the features of strong READMEs and the common pitfalls of weak
    ones.
-   Plan, write and check a README for a dataset, using a list of recommended
    content.
-   Describe what a README for code needs, including installation, usage,
    licence and contact details.

## About the organisers
This workshop was designed as a joint venture between the BES Journal of Methods in Ecology and Evolution and the [UKRI Digital Research Skills Catalyst](https://digitalskillscatalyst.ac.uk/).
